text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - Bund futures off early highs, but still holding gains above 101.00 level. U.S. industrial production due at 1415 GMT. Bund/T-note spread steady at 45 basis points. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.03, up 0.07 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts slipped off the day's high ahead of the close on light profit-taking but settled 8/32 up on the day. Market made up some more lost ground against Bunds but dealers said the spread not likely to narrow further next week. PSBR on Monday main focus. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-04/32, up 10/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - December bond future ends week near contract high with overseas bond markets providing impetus. Volume low on Friday. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 127.62 down 0.04 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds, futures opted for a quieter end to week after galloping ahead in recent days. Traders say foreigners still buying on dips but others say market might be contemplating forming a top. Budget voting due to end Saturday in lower house. Lots of speculation about timing of lira's possible return to ERM. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.56 up 0.10 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries widen losses after U of Mich sentiment gains. U Mich preliminary November consumer sentiment jumps to 98.9 vs. 96.5 Oct final, current conditions 107.0 vs. 106.6 Oct, expectations 93.7 vs. 89.9 Oct final - market sources. October industrial production drop showed manufacturing weak.The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 115-10/32, up 1/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.42 percent.

JAPAN - Key December Japanese Goverment Bonds (JGB) futures ended higher, due to position adjustment by dealers ahead of the weekend, a brokerage trader said. Traders said investors were said to have bought long-term cash JGBs, which also supported the market.In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 124.76, up 0.31 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Attention on Friday turned to the Russian roadshow which hits London today ahead of the expected launch of its debut Eurobond of up to $500 million. Meanwhile the primary market saw a stream of new issue activity with a number of highly-structured deals launched. In dollars, BFCE set a $125 million step-up perp FRN, while Huntington National Bank issued a $250 million five-year FRN. Scottish life set a 125 million stg perpetual bond. Morgan Stanley led a 100 million mark April 2012 Brazil repackaged step-down bonds.
